title: Shared or Exclusive
goal: Learn the aliasing rule that governs mutable and shared borrowing.

sections.text: You know that borrowing with `&` lets you read data without taking ownership. When you need to modify borrowed data, you use a mutable reference, written `&mut`.

sections.caption: `&mut` gives permission to modify the value through the reference.

sections.text: Rust enforces one core rule for borrowing to prevent data corruption. At any given moment, you can have many shared `&` references, or exactly one exclusive `&mut` reference.

sections.caption: You cannot create `&mut val` while shared reference `r1` is still alive.

sections.text: The compiler checks this rule at compile time and rejects conflicts with error `E0502` or `E0499`. This rule eliminates data races and iterator invalidation bugs entirely.
Lifetimes and borrowing across struct fields are covered later in this deck.

explanation: Learn the aliasing rule that governs mutable and shared borrowing.
